items.title: Kosuke Kawamura Turns Legendary ‘COBRA’ Manga Into a ¥3.5 Million JPY Contemporary Artwork
items.text: Kosuke Kawamura Turns Legendary ‘COBRA’ Manga Into a ¥3.5 Million JPY Contemporary Artwork Toei and TANGLE have officially launched the ReVIBES Project, a new collaborative initiative that reimagines some of Japan's most iconic IPs through contemporary art. Moving beyond nostalgia and conventional collaborations, the project transforms beloved classics into collectible artworks, introducing them to a new generation of collectors and the global art marketFor its inaugural edition, the project tapped internationally renowned collage artist, graphic designer, and art director Kosuke Kawamura to deconstruct and reassemble COBRA — Buichi Terasawa’s legendary sci-fi manga classic. The resulting two physical art pieces made their high-profile auction debut in Tokyo, fetching a combined ¥3.5 million JPY (approx. $24,000 USD). As Hiroto Munakata, representative of TANGLE and the mastermind behind the project's concept, explains: “This is not about reviving IP, but about reconstructing its value. We are not selling nostalgia — we want to show how masterpieces can be updated for the present day.”Why COBRA?First serialized in Weekly Shonen Jump in 1978, COBRA follows a rogue space pirate armed with a psychological, arm-embedded "Psycho-Gun". Infusing a singular universe with hard-boiled storytelling, cosmic action, and sharp humor, the manga immediately became a cornerstone of Japanese pop culture and has since been translated into over a dozen languages.Crucially, creator Buichi Terasawa was a legendary innovator who pioneered the integration of computer graphics into comic production, famously coining the term “digital manga”. Reinterpreting this exact spirit of technical disruption through a modern artistic lens forms the perfect foundation for ReVIBES Project.For Toei, the initiative represents a vital method for archival management. “No matter how great a work may be, the passage of time can gradually reduce it to something known only by a dedicated few,” notes Rintaro Shimatani of Toei. “Through ReVIBES Project, we believe these works can reach audiences they never had the opportunity to connect with before.”Kosuke Kawamura’s DeconstructionKnown for his cross-disciplinary portfolio spanning fashion, street culture, music and advertising, Kosuke Kawamura was uniquely suited to bridge the gap between subculture and high art. items.title: NikeSKIMS Wraps the Split-Toe Air Rift in Satin for Its "Obsidian" and "Night Silver" Pair
items.text: NikeSKIMS Wraps the Split-Toe Air Rift in Satin for Its "Obsidian" and "Night Silver" Pair Name: NikeSKIMS Air Rift SatinColorway: Obsidian, Night Silver/Base Grey-Medium SilverSKU: IQ7158-002, IQ7158-400MSRP: $160 USDRelease Date: July 30Where to Buy: Nike, SKIMSThe NikeSKIMS Rift Satin gives one of Nike's most divisive silhouettes a new lease on life, dressing the split-toe Air Rift in satin-like panels across a pair of colorways for the Studio Edit 02 collection. Offered in "Obsidian" and "Night Silver," the release keeps the model's unmistakable low-profile shape while refining its surface into something sleeker and more polished for Kim Kardashian’s SKIMS.For this iteration, the changes are focused on material and finish rather than structure. Satin-like panels give the Rift a cleaner, more elevated look without altering the low-profile shape that defines the model. The split-toe forefoot remains the centerpiece, while an adjustable strap runs across the midfoot to lock in the fit, a functional nod to the original's cinching system. Underfoot, the segmented outsole carries over, preserving the flexible, articulated feel that made the first Rift move so closely with the foot.The SKIMS colorways lean in different directions. The "Obsidian" pair takes a darker, moodier route, while the "Night Silver" version runs a tonal arrangement of Night Silver, Base Grey, and Medium Silver, stacking closely related metallic shades into a near-monochrome finish that plays into the ongoing appetite for silver footwear. Both treatments let the satin paneling do the talking, keeping branding minimal and the focus squarely on the silhouette's distinctive geometry.The Air Rift has always been a shoe defined by its silhouette. Nike introduced the model in 1996, drawing on the split-toe construction of the Japanese tabi and the barefoot efficiency of Kenyan distance runners, and the result was a minimal, glove-like runner unlike anything else in the catalog. That divisive, fashion-forward shape has made it a recurring favorite in cycles where minimalism and Y2K styling return to the forefront, and its reappearance under the NikeSKIMS banner slots neatly into that pattern. items.title: Apple's New Upgrade Program Lets You Lease an iPhone, Mac, or iPad Starting at $17.99 USD Monthly
items.text: Apple's New Upgrade Program Lets You Lease an iPhone, Mac, or iPad Starting at $17.99 USD Monthly Summary Apple has officially introduced Apple Upgrade, a new US-based leasing program for iPhone, Mac, iPad and Apple Watch modelsDeveloped in partnership with Klarna, the service offers 12- and 24-month terms for iPhones and Watches alongside 24- and 36-month terms for Macs and iPadsThe program replaces the existing iPhone Upgrade Program and provides options to upgrade early, purchase the device or return it at the end of the lease Apple has launched "Apple Upgrade," a comprehensive hardware leasing program designed to provide a more accessible entry point for its latest ecosystem of devices. Rolling out across the brand's online and physical stores in the United States, the service arrives just weeks after the tech giant hiked prices on its MacBooks and iPads amid ongoing industry component shortages. Now, users can lease an iPhone 17e starting at $17.99 USD per month, an Apple Watch Series 11 or iPad Air for $11.99 USD per month and a MacBook Air for $24.99 USD per month.Developed in partnership with financial provider Klarna, the service requires a soft credit check for approval and operates much like a standard vehicle lease. Customers commit to 12- or 24-month terms for iPhones and Apple Watches, while Mac and iPad plans extend to 24 or 36 months. At the end of the selected term, users can trade their device in for a next-generation model, buy the hardware outright with a one-time payment or simply return the product and exit the ecosystem entirely. To lower monthly costs, participants can integrate their existing hardware through Apple Trade In or earn three percent Daily Cash back by paying with an Apple Card.The new initiative effectively phases out the decade-old iPhone Upgrade Program, which is no longer accepting new enrollments. A critical shift in the transition is the removal of bundled AppleCare coverage, a feature previously baked into the legacy mobile leasing plan. Furthermore, the brand appears to be establishing strict guardrails to ensure consistent payments. Code discovered in early beta builds of iOS 27 suggests developers are preparing a restricted mode capable of locking financed devices out of specific applications if accounts fall into arrears. items.title: Starbucks Japan Turns Its Menu Into Blind Box Collectible Plush Charms With the "Joyful Capsule" Series
items.text: Starbucks Japan Turns Its Menu Into Blind Box Collectible Plush Charms With the "Joyful Capsule" Series Starbucks Japan is stepping into capsule-toy territory for the first time with the Starbucks Joyful Capsule, a run of palm-sized plush charms shaped like the chain's most recognizable menu items. Sold through blind capsules under the concept "Starbucks Charm with Warmth," the collectibles arrive August 2, a date the company marks as the anniversary of its arrival in Japan.The concept plugs directly into one of Japan's most entrenched retail rituals. Gachapon, the capsule-toy vending machines that dispense a random collectible for a set price, have been a fixture of Japanese consumer culture for decades, and the blind-box format they pioneered has since become a global engine for hype-driven collecting, from designer vinyl figures to the plush-charm boom that brands now chase. By issuing its first capsule toy through this system, Starbucks is borrowing a mechanic built for repeat pulls and trade-driven community, the same surprise-and-collect logic that has powered so many recent drop phenomena.The products themselves lean on that collectible instinct. The standard lineup comprises five designs, each a plush rendering of a Starbucks staple: a Double Tall Latte in a To Go cup, a Caramel Macchiato in a For Here glass, a TOKYO Roast, a Matcha Cream Frappuccino, and a Sugar Donut. Every capsule contains one charm at random, so buyers only learn which they have pulled once the roughly 75mm shell cracks open. Each charm carries a hook, a small but deliberate design choice that lets collectors chain favorites together or clip them onto bags and pouches, extending the appeal from a single pull into a modular, mix-and-match set.Timing gives the drop added resonance. Starbucks entered the Japanese market three decades ago, and the brand has grown into one of the country's most culturally embedded foreign imports, its seasonal Frappuccinos and regional exclusives treated with the kind of anticipation usually reserved for streetwear. items.text: Palm Angels Wants You To Explore the “Lost Frames” in Its FW26 Campaign Summary Palm Angels unveils its FW26 "Lost Frames" campaign, lensed in a historic theatre using a grainy VHS aesthetic.The range updates signature tracksuits, technical outerwear, tailoring and fluid mini dresses with rich fabrications.The collection is now available via Palm Angels and select global retailers. Palm Angels’ Fall/Winter 2026 campaign, titled “Lost Frames,” unfolds as a cinematic exploration of memory and atmosphere. Shot by Sharna Osbourne and Van Khokhlov inside a historic theatre, the visuals, defined by Osbourne’s VHS aesthetic, capture empty auditoriums, backstage corners and softly lit interiors, creating a tactile, timeworn quality that blurs the line between performance and aftermath.The narrative unfolds across empty auditoriums, backstage corners, and velvet-draped balconies, creating an intimate, lingering post-show atmosphere. Users attempting to generate text mimicking the specific style of famous authors are now hitting a digital brick wall. ChatGPT is explicitly declining direct prompts to clone the literary voices of prominent writers. The system points to copyright protections for both living and deceased creators when blocking these requests.Testing conducted by Ars Technica and the research publication No Latency first highlighted the behavioral shift. When prompted to channel Agatha Christie for a mystery story, the chatbot refuses the direct imitation. It offers a compromise instead. items.title: A Vow Written in Scent: Inside AVAU’s First Permanent Space in Milan
items.text: A Vow Written in Scent: Inside AVAU’s First Permanent Space in Milan Summary AVAU opens its first boutique in Milan's Brera district.Designed with Crosby Studios, the space merges historic details with stainless steel.Features include a Vatican fresco-inspired sofa and a central "Magic Tray". Italian fragrance house AVAU has officially opened its first permanent home at Via Fiori Chiari 7 in Milan's historic Brera district. Founded by siblings Leonardo, Carolina and Caterina Catalani - who bring three generations of family perfumery heritage to the venture - the brand's name serves as the phonetic expression of "A Vow." Rooted in the Catalani siblings’ family heritage, the boutique reflects AVAU’s guiding principle of “A Promise Made Scent,” offering visitors an immersive environment that encourages conversation, discovery and connection.In a notable creative collaboration, AVAU partnered with designer Harry Nuriev and his multidisciplinary practice Crosby Studios to bring the space to life. The interior design establishes a striking dialogue between heritage and contemporary craftsmanship, where original walls, exposed timber beams and a restored fireplace coexist with sleek stainless steel work surfaces and laboratory-inspired fixtures. Upon entering, visitors are greeted by a living room anchored by a bespoke sofa. Its upholstery is inspired by the frescoes of Vatican City, paying homage to the founders' grandparents, who once operated a perfumery inside the Vatican.Opposite the living room sits the "Magic Tray," a prominent display showcasing the house's collection of six fragrances. This design feature recreates a cherished family ritual from the founders' childhood, when their mother would ask each morning which fragrance they had chosen to wear for the day. The kitchen also serves as the symbolic heart of the Home, where ideas are exchanged and the brand’s creative vision continues to evolve.AVAU ParfumVia Fiori Chiari, 7, 20121 Milano MI, Italy View this post on Instagram A post shared by AVAU (@avauparfum) Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.text: Lalique Opens First Directly Operated Osaka Boutique at QUARTZ SHINSAIBASHI Summary Lalique opens its first directly operated Kansai boutique at QUARTZ SHINSAIBASHI.Spanning 106 square meters, the space features integrated crystal panels, suspended Champs-Elysées installations and iconic vases alongside Japan-inspired collections. Lalique has opened its first directly operated boutique in Osaka, located at QUARTZ Shinsaibashi, marking a significant milestone in the Maison’s expansion in Japan. The new space introduces Lalique’s full creative universe to the Kansai region for the first time, reflecting the brand’s commitment to immersive retail environments and closer client relationships. Set in the vibrant Shinsaibashi district, the boutique is conceived as more than a retail space, designed to showcase crystal through light, transparency, and texture.Spanning 106 square meters, the boutique features crystal panels with motifs such as Lauriers and Merles et Raisins, alongside a suspended Champs-Elysées liana installation. Iconic creations including Bacchantes, Mossi and Tourbillons are displayed alongside Pivoines, Plumes, and Lalique’s signature animal sculptures. Collections inspired by cherry blossoms, such as Fleurs de Cerisier and Sakura, echo Japanese cultural motifs and highlight René Lalique’s enduring dialogue with nature. The boutique also presents the full breadth of Lalique’s universe, from crystal vases and decorative objects to jewellery, fragrances, and architectural pieces like chandeliers and interior panels.The Osaka opening also marks the Japan debut of Lalique’s collaboration with Fromental, the renowned handcrafted wallpaper house. These designs enrich the boutique with a new layer of depth, establishing a dialogue between crystal and decorative arts.Lalique Shinsaibashi3F, Quartz Shinsaibashi, 3 Chome−12−14Minamisenba Chuo Ward, Osaka,〒542-0081, Japan Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.text: MING and Royal Selangor Tap Local Pewter Craft for the All-New 37.06 Watch Summary MING and Royal Selangor debut the 88-piece 37.06 Titanium Watch.It features a hand-hammered pewter dial made in Kuala Lumpur.Retailing for CHF 5,000, it marks MING's first locally assembled timepiece. The partnership brings together Royal Selangor’s 140‑year heritage in pewter craftsmanship with MING’s contemporary design language, resulting in a timepiece that is both culturally rooted and visually distinctive.The dial, produced in Kuala Lumpur, showcases pewter’s natural depth and texture, catching light differently from every angle to give each watch a unique character. items.title: TAG Heuer, Team Ikuzawa and Bamford Reunite for a 150-Piece Carrera Chronograph
items.text: TAG Heuer, Team Ikuzawa and Bamford Reunite for a 150-Piece Carrera Chronograph Summary TAG Heuer, Team Ikuzawa \and Bamford release a collaborative Carrera Chronograph, limited to 150 pieces.The design draws inspiration from '70s- '80s Roadmaster stopwatches, but reinterpreted with modern features.Priced at $10,500 USD, the watch is now available via TAG Heuer. TAG Heuer has reunited with Japanese racing icon Team Ikuzawa and Bamford Watch Department for a new collaborative Carrera Chronograph. Following their initial 2023 collaboration, this new limited-edition release channels the visual codes of 1970s and 1980s Japanese motorsport through a contemporary lens. Spearheaded by Team Principal Mai Ikuzawa alongside George Bamford, the project draws direct creative inspiration from the Team Ikuzawa archive, specifically reinterpreting the graphic aesthetic and high legibility of the team's historic Roadmaster stopwatch.Housed in a 39mm fine-brushed and polished steel "Glassbox" case, the timepiece boasts a bezel-free construction and domed sapphire crystal, offering an uninterrupted view of the dial. The white dial features a textured Clou de Paris finish and printed numeral indexes that mimic vintage timing instruments. Highlighting the team's signature color palette, bold red accents appear on the lacquered hour and minute hands, central chronograph seconds hand, red-printed 3 o'clock minute counter and a dedicated date disc at 6 o'clock.Powering the watch is the in-house Calibre TH20-10 automatic chronograph movement, which intentionally omits a running seconds subdial. This specific 2-counter layout leaves the 6 o'clock dial space open for the prominent Team Ikuzawa logo, paying homage to vintage 1960s and 1970s racing chronographs. The watch is delivered on a 7-row steel bracelet and comes bundled as a set with two additional interchangeable straps: a white perforated leather strap with red stitching inspired by classic driving gloves, and a red-and-white striped textile strap referencing Team Ikuzawa's racing livery. Its custom sapphire caseback is engraved with "TEAM IKUZAWA", "BAMFORD WATCH DEPARTMENT," alongside its individual issue number.The Carrera Chronograph x Team Ikuzawa is presented in custom packaging designed to emjlate a pit garage toolbox, alongside a travel pouch and branded charms. items.text: Six Flags Is Building "Bakunawa," a Record-Breaking Spinning Giga Coaster Summary Six Flags Great Adventure unveiled Bakunawa, a record-breaking spinning giga coaster inspired by Philippine mythology slated to open in 2027The ride will feature world-record-setting statistics including a 382-foot height, 100-mph top speed and the first floorless spinning coaster trainsBakunawa serves as the centerpiece of a multi-year transformation for the park's Boardwalk district Six Flags Great Adventure has officially revealed Bakunawa, a massive new attraction set to become the world's tallest and fastest spinning roller coaster when it opens in 2027. Named after a legendary sea serpent from Philippine mythology, the giga coaster serves as the culmination of the park's highly anticipated Project Purple teaser campaign. The addition represents a major investment in the resort's ongoing transformation of its Boardwalk district.Bakunawa is engineered to shatter six world records. Riders will experience the fastest inversion at 80 mph and the first upside-down launch in coaster history. Utilizing free-spinning and floorless 20-passenger trains that rotate independently throughout the two-minute and 17-second journey, the attraction aims to provide a unique visual and physical sensation for every passenger across its 3,163 feet of track. The coaster features three distinct linear synchronous motor launches, beginning with an initial blast from zero to 60 mph.After ascending high above the park, a final launch will propel guests to an exhilarating 100 mph before plunging down a 382-foot drop. The layout also incorporates the world's longest stall inversion and a sweeping 180-degree bank spiral that offers sweeping views of the surrounding New Jersey landscape. To board Bakunawa, guests will need to meet a minimum height requirement of 48 inches. Park officials anticipate the massive structure will join an elite class of giga coasters globally.The monumental project acts as the signature anchor for a revitalized seashore-themed area at the property. Representatives position the record-breaking construction as a defining milestone in a broader strategy to solidify the location as a premier regional destination for thrill-seekers. The nearby grounds recently received five new family attractions and introduced seasonal nighttime entertainment to encourage visitors to spend more time exploring the modernized space. items.title: Michael B. Jordan Steals to Right Old Wrongs in Teaser for ‘The Thomas Crown Affair’
items.text: Michael B. Jordan Steals to Right Old Wrongs in Teaser for ‘The Thomas Crown Affair’ Summary Michael B. Jordan directs, produces and stars in Amazon MGM's reimagining of 'The Thomas Crown Affair,' the third screen take on the art-thief storyHis version rewrites the character's motive, sending Crown after stolen or sold artifacts to return them to their rightful creatorsAdria Arjona plays the former FBI agent tracking him heist by heist while Kenneth Branagh circles as a looming threat Amazon MGM Studios has released the trailer for The Thomas Crown Affair, Michael B. Jordan's reimagining of the billionaire art-thief story that puts a pointed new spin on the character's heists. Jordan directs and stars as Crown in the third screen iteration of the tale, and the footage frames the theft less as a rich man's sport than as a mission with a conscience.The reframe is the whole point. Where earlier versions cast Crown as a wealthy thrill-seeker, Jordan's take gives him a cause: his true aim is to return precious stolen or sold artifacts to the people who created them. That motive reshapes the cat-and-mouse structure the franchise is known for, with Adria Arjona playing the former FBI agent hunting Crown heist by heist and Kenneth Branagh lurking as an insidious antagonist threatening to bring him down. The result reads as a heist thriller with its moral compass deliberately recalibrated.Jordan has been explicit about why he rebuilt the story from the ground up. He told Variety in November, “I didn’t want a reboot. I wanted a reimagination. The first two films were about rich white guys stealing for fun. That doesn’t land today.” He continued, “Ours is more personal. The stakes are higher. Still got the fashion, romance.”The production carries a notable pedigree behind the camera as well. Drew Pearce wrote the script from a previous draft by Wes Tooke and Justin Britt-Gibson, working from the 1968 original that starred Steve McQueen and Faye Dunaway, the film later remade in 1999 with Pierce Brosnan and Rene Russo. Jordan produces alongside Elizabeth Raposo for Outlier Society, with Charles Roven for Atlas Entertainment, plus Patrick McCormick and Toberoff Productions' Marc Toberoff. Alan Trustman, who wrote the original film, executive produces. The trailer first debuted at CinemaCon in April, arriving with Jordan fresh off his Best Actor Oscar win for Sinners, his first Academy nomination and victory, earned for Ryan Coogler's vampire horror film.Watch the tease

items.title: Thuso Mbedu Summons the Magic of Orïsha in the First 'Children of Blood and Bone’ Trailer
items.text: Thuso Mbedu Summons the Magic of Orïsha in the First 'Children of Blood and Bone’ Trailer Summary Paramount's first look at 'Children of Blood and Bone' introduces Thuso Mbedu as Zélie, a young warrior fighting to restore magic to the kingdom of OrïshaThe ensemble stacks Damson Idris, Amandla Stenberg, Chiwetel Ejiofor, Regina King, Idris Elba, Cynthia Erivo and Viola Davis beneath director Gina Prince-BythewoodTems and Burna Boy anchor the film's music while the trailer moves to an excerpt of Beyoncé's "Energy" Paramount Pictures has dropped the first trailer for Children of Blood and Bone, the big-screen adaptation of Tomi Adeyemi's 2018 bestseller, and it lands with the scale of a full-blown blockbuster. The clip pulls back the curtain on Orïsha, a mythic pre-colonial West African kingdom where magic has been violently stripped from the people, and centers Thuso Mbedu as Zélie Adebola, the young maji at the heart of the fight to bring it back.The footage wastes no time flexing its ambition. Sweeping location photography, large-scale battle sequences and creature-heavy VFX build out a world divided into clans, each wielding its own elemental gift, from those who bend water, fire, wind and earth to seers who can read the past and future. Mbedu's Zélie, gifted with the power to command undead spirits, moves through it all as a coming-of-age heroine dodging the forces of a ruthless king, played by Backrooms star Chiwetel Ejiofor.Behind the camera is Gina Prince-Bythewood, returning to the epic register she commanded on The Woman King, and she brings collaborators with her: Mbedu, Viola Davis and Lashana Lynch all reunite from that 2022 hit. The rest of the call sheet reads like a fantasy fan's wish list. Damson Idris and Amandla Stenberg play the king's children, Prince Inan and Princess Amari, while Tosin Cole, Regina King, Idris Elba and Cynthia Erivo round out a genuinely stacked ensemble.Then there's the sound. Paramount has loaded the project with serious musical firepower, tapping Tems as executive music producer and Burna Boy as executive music consultant, both attached to deliver original songs. The trailer itself rides an excerpt of Beyoncé's 2022 track "Energy," a needle-drop that signals exactly how big this swing is meant to feel.Watch the trailer above. Children of Blood and Bone opens in theaters and IMAX on January 15, 2027. Read more at Hypebeast

items.text: McDonald's China Rebuilds Its Takeaway Bag Into the Fry-Toting "Big Fries Backpack" Summary McDonald's China has turned its instantly recognizable brown paper takeaway bag into a wearable backpack for the 12th edition of Big Fries DayThe build layers on functional detailing, from Velcro fry-carton side pockets to a padded interior sized for a laptopThe design began as a fan's handmade tribute before McDonald's China developed it into an official product McDonald's China has turned its most familiar piece of packaging into a bag you can actually wear, and the Big Fries Backpack commits to the bit at every seam. Rather than slap a logo onto a blank silhouette, the brand modeled the whole thing on the brown paper takeaway bag that leaves the counter with every order, then engineered in enough real utility to move it past pure novelty.The construction starts with the shell. The exterior uses a lightweight DuPont paper material chosen to mimic the crinkle and texture of a genuine takeaway bag, printed with the Golden Arches up front alongside fry graphics and folded-bag detailing that sell the illusion. A detachable charm shaped like a McDonald's order receipt dangles off the body, while the zipper pulls are molded to resemble individual fries dipped in ketchup, so even the smallest touchpoints stay on theme.The most eye-catching engineering sits on the sides. A pair of red pockets shaped like McDonald's fry cartons attach to either flank with Velcro and are built to hold actual fries, though McDonald's leaves the wisdom of pressing greasy food against a paper-textured bag to the owner. Those pockets pull off cleanly when a slimmer profile is wanted, and the interior hides a compartment reserved specifically for ketchup packets, a small but telling nod to how completely the design maps to the ordering ritual.Where the exterior leans into spectacle, the inside gets practical. The main compartment is fitted with dividers and sized to take a 13- or 14-inch laptop, which reframes the backpack as a viable daily commuter rather than a one-off gag. The shoulder strap continues the theme with a holder built to keep a fry carton upright, a detail that reads as either clever ergonomics or a public statement of priorities depending on your appetite.The Big Fries Backpack is available exclusively via McDonald’s China. The ultra-durable textile is produced by Fothergill - a historic British manufacturer supplying protective gear to the military since 1847 - and is specifically designed to resist oils, ozone, weathering, flame and chemical exposure. Built to tackle extreme weather with a touch of existential dread, the coat comes packaged inside its own custom garment bag crafted from the very same chemical-suit fabric.Beyond its construction, the FWAHBL Jacket arrives as part of a larger fictional universe. Each piece ships in retro video game-inspired packaging, accompanied by a Marvel-style comic strip and a film-style trailer, with a playable game currently in development. This narrative-driven approach transforms the jacket into more than functional apparel — it becomes a collectible artifact that merges fashion, gaming, and storytelling. While not certified safety equipment, the jacket is designed for extreme weather and existential dread, reflecting Vollebak’s ethos of creating clothing for the challenges of the future.Priced at $3,995 USD, the FWAHBL Jacket is available via Vollebak's official website. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Vollebak (@vollebak) Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.text: Sotheby's Maison Presents Major Yayoi Kusama Career Retrospective Exhibition Summary Sotheby's Salon in Hong Kong presents a major exhibition celebrating the seven-decade career of artist Yayoi KusamaThe curated showcase features rare works spanning the 1950s to 2010s across three thematic sectionsThe exhibition is currently open at Sotheby's Maison through August 20, 2026 Sotheby’s Salon has officially opened a major exhibition celebrating legendary Japanese artist Yayoi Kusama at 1/F, Sotheby’s Maison in Hong Kong's The Landmark. Tracing seven decades of influential output, the retrospective highlights paintings, works on paper, and screenprints spanning from the 1950s to the 2010s.Organized into three distinct thematic sections—Nature and Nurture, Fauna and Flora, and The Urban and Pop—the exhibition charts Kusama's artistic evolution from her formative years in Japan through her groundbreaking period in the United States and her return home. Key early highlights include The Pacific Ocean No. A.B.X. (1959), a rare ink, pastel, and gouache work executed shortly after her arrival in New York.The showcase also features canvas pieces such as Sunset Grapes (1988), which transforms organic forms into vibrant patterns of repetition, and the rarely seen Handbag (1984), demonstrating her engagement with consumer culture, fashion, and everyday objects. Together with examples of her celebrated Infinity Nets, pumpkins, and floral imagery, the selection offers a comprehensive view of the artist's enduring visual universe.The Yayoi Kusama exhibition is currently open to the public at 1/F, Sotheby’s Maison, running through August 20, 2026.Sotheby's Maison1/F, LANDMARK CHATER8 Connaught Road CentralCentral, Hong Kong Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.title: PARCO Unveils Its 2026 Fall/Winter Campaign, "NOSTALGIC FUTURE"
items.text: PARCO Unveils Its 2026 Fall/Winter Campaign, "NOSTALGIC FUTURE" PARCO, which not only operates fashion buildings in Japan but also promotes cutting-edge culture through venues such as theaters, cinemas, and live music halls, has unveiled its advertising campaign for the Fall/Winter 2026 season built around the concept of "NOSTALGIC FUTURE."Serving as creative director is Christophe Brunnquell, one of Europe's foremost creatives, who spent 15 years as the founding art director of Purple, the storied independent French fashion magazine. At the heart of the "NOSTALGIC FUTURE" concept is LE COEUR JAPONAIS (The Japanese Heart), a book published in 1927 by Brunnquell's great-grandfather, the philosopher and writer Félicien Challaye. Written after Challaye's travels through Japan, the book reflects his fascination with the spirituality and virtues of the Japanese people. Its enduring portrait of the Japanese spirit, along with its ideas connecting West and East, memory and future, forms the creative foundation of this campaign nearly a hundred years later.The campaign is set within a Western-style mansion on the outskirts of Paris. Casting both Eastern and Western models, and framing them amid scattered books, sculptures that carry a sense of history, and antique furniture, the visuals fuse elements drawn from the past with staging that looks toward the future, constructing a world that belongs to no single era. The result is imagery in which distinct timelines appear to intersect within a single frame. Equally striking is the way the passage of time is expressed through color, shifting from autumnal looks centered on ecru and navy toward winter looks defined by deep reds and magentas.Speaking about the project, Brunnquell commented, "I believe the future is always built from memories, traditions, and stories that existed before us." He described nostalgia not as a simple act of looking back, but as "a creative force for imagining the future," explaining that he built the campaign by weaving together his own roots and his respect for Japanese culture.Taking a single book written nearly 100 years ago as its point of departure, PARCO's 2026 Fall/Winter campaign, "NOSTALGIC FUTURE," presents a worldview that moves fluidly across past and future, West and East. items.text: LinkedIn Introduces New "Seems Like AI Slop" Reporting Button to Combat Feed Spam Summary LinkedIn launched a user reporting tool that allows members to flag feed content as "Seems like AI slop" to combat machine-generated spam.The platform is officially retiring its AI-driven post enhancement feature and introducing a proofreading tool that preserves the original author's voice.New backend classifiers and profile verification rollouts aim to clean up the professional network after reports showed massive spikes in automated posts. LinkedIn is officially pushing back against the flood of machine-generated feed spam. The professional networking platform rolled out a new reporting button that allows users to flag content specifically as "Seems like AI slop." Tucked inside the standard three-dot menu on any post, the tool lets human readers police the timeline. The move marks a direct response to a growing cultural frustration with synthetic engagement bait that has increasingly dominated the site.Chief Product Officer Hari Srinivasan announced the measures directly, noting that authentic human connection remains the core focus for the company. To support the user-facing reporting button, LinkedIn is ramping up backend classifiers designed to detect low-quality automation before it hits the feed. The system is already working overtime. According to Srinivasan, the platform currently blocks hundreds of thousands of automated comment attempts daily and has thwarted billions of broad automation actions over the past few months alone.The company is also walking back some of its own previous AI integrations. LinkedIn is removing a tool that offered to "enhance" user posts with artificial intelligence. In its place, the platform will introduce a standard proofreading feature built to check spelling and grammar while preserving the original voice of the author. For creators, the backend analytics dashboard will soon test a private flagging system. If multiple users report a specific post as inauthentic or heavily reliant on AI, the original author will receive a quiet notification.The anti-slop campaign arrives just as third-party data paints a stark picture of the network's current state. A recent study by AI detection firm Pangram revealed that 41 percent of long-form posts on LinkedIn registered as completely machine-written. items.text: Le Labo Dedicates “SHIU 25” City Exclusive Scent to Beijing’s Sacred Courtyards Summary Le Labo's SHIU 25 anchors powdery iris, olibanum and warm woods around the serene, balancing Shiu note.The scent draws inspiration from Beijing's He Yuan Lab, a restored Siheyuan courtyard blending wabi-sabi aesthetics with ancient heritage.Available exclusively in Beijing year-round, it'll be available globally for a limited time. Le Labo expands its coveted City Exclusive Collection with SHIU 25, an Eau de Parfum dedicated to the city of Beijing. Conceived as an homage to traditional spaces built for quietude and inner return, the fragrance captures the soul of the house's historic Beijing He Yuan Lab — a culturally protected Siheyuan courtyard nestled in House 19 at Wang Fu Central.Global Brand President and Creative Director Deborah Royer describes the creation as "an invitation to find centered calm, self-reflection, and a moment of pause in a world that rarely grants one". In this intentionally compact composition, ethereal notes of powdery iris and sacred olibanum float weightlessly above a grounding foundation of warm, anchoring woods. The experience unfolds like a serene walk through hidden courtyard gardens, where gentle shadows dance across well-worn wooden floors and the creative spirit awakens in sacred silence. items.text: 'The Devil Wears Prada 2' Understands Exactly What It Needs to Be The world didn't necessarily need a sequel to The Devil Wears Prada. It’s not a criticism, just a fact about revisiting a movie that ended exactly where it needed to. And yet, 20 years later, David Frankel and writer Aline Brosh McKenna have uncovered a narrative premise that actually justifies reopening the doors of Runway: a media industry collapsing under its own weight and the people who build their careers in the twilight of its golden years refusing to be quietly consumed by it.The Devil Wears Prada 2's setup alone handles so much heavy lifting. Andy Sachs (Anne Hathaway) the award-winning investigative journalist, loses her job with a text — the universe’s passive-aggressive, late-stage-capitalist answer to a final dismissal. Miranda Priestly (Meryl Streep) finds herself scrambling to adapt to a digitally focused media landscape and staring down a forced retirement. Emily Charlton (Emily Blunt), Miranda's former first assistant who approaches the idea of a trip to Paris as if she were commanding troops, reinvents herself as a powerhouse Dior executive who has the kind of revenue Miranda is suddenly dependent upon. And if this power triangle sounds uncannily familiar to any recent media professional, then good, you’ve been paying attention. That is the core insight this film has: what’s the worst thing about media becoming a wasteland? It's not the layoffs or the ever-shrinking masthead. It’s seeing everyone who cemented this status quo utterly bested.The magic is the script does not force a sentimental decline of Miranda. Streep plays her as someone the last 20 years have merely honed, who has ceded her ego’s more monstrous impulses for an amplified sense of conviction. It’s such a subtle, believable transformation, and only a transformation as nuanced as this one would have held. The fashion is, as it should be, something to talk about on its own. Costume designer Molly Rogers (who also worked on the Sex and the City spinoff ...And Just Like That) steps in to replace legendary Patricia Field, creating thought selections with deliberate intentionality. Miranda's weathered Dries Van Noten toreador jacket, trimmed with the perfect turquoise, is a prime example of the garment’s ability to reward a deeper view. items.text: Billie Eilish's "Eilish Intense" Eau de Parfum Deepens Its Amber Gourmand Into a Nighttime Signature Summary Eilish Intense amplifies the original Eilish Eau de Parfum with a richer, more enveloping take on its amber gourmand profileThe composition moves from red berries and mandarin through creamy vanilla and cocoa into a dry down of warm musks, tonka bean, and woodsThe collection's sculptural bust-inspired bottle is reimagined in a luminous radiant gold to mirror the scent's intensified warmth Eilish Fragrances has unveiled Eilish Intense, a deeper evolution of Billie Eilish's award-winning debut scent developed in partnership with Parlux. Rather than reinvent the formula, Intense amplifies the warmth and sensuality of the original amber gourmand, reworking its structure into a fuller, more enveloping expression built for after-dark wear.The composition opens on a luminous contrast of red berries and mandarin, wrapped in what the brand describes as the textural sweetness of sugared petals. From there it moves into a heart of creamy vanilla, soft spices, and cocoa, the trio responsible for the addictive richness that defines the scent's middle stretch. The dry down is where Intense earns its name, settling into warm musks, tonka bean, and sleek woods that linger against the skin. It is a recognizable extension of the original's creamy vanilla signature, tuned for depth rather than novelty, and Eilish herself has framed the split plainly: the original for daytime, Intense for night.The bottle carries the concept in physical form. Eilish Intense retains the collection's sculptural silhouette, an abstract interpretation of the human bust, now finished in a luminous radiant gold chosen to reflect the fragrance's intensified warmth. The design leans on Eilish's stated view of fragrance bottles as standalone objects, and the outer carton extends the treatment with gold and iridescent detailing that reinforces the collection's richer visual world.The sustainability credentials remain consistent with the rest of the line. Eilish Intense is vegan, paraben-free, and formulated with clean ingredients, while the carton is printed with Envirofoil and produced using 100 percent renewable wind energy. items.title: The 2027 Met Gala Will Be All About John Galliano
items.text: The 2027 Met Gala Will Be All About John Galliano Summary The Metropolitan Museum of Art has announced that John Galliano will be the subject of its spring 2027 Costume Institute exhibitionTitled John Galliano Horizons the exhibition marks the first major museum retrospective examining the full breadth of his four-decade careerThe show will be on view at The Met Fifth Avenue from May 9 2027 through January 9 2028 The Metropolitan Museum of Art has officially announced that John Galliano will be the subject of its landmark Spring 2027 Costume Institute exhibition as well as the Met Gala, titled John Galliano: Horizons. Galliano becomes only the third living designer in history to receive a solo exhibition at The Met, following Yves Saint Laurent in 1983 and Rei Kawakubo in 2017.Curated by Andrew Bolton, Curator in Charge of The Costume Institute, the retrospective spans Galliano’s career from his 1984 Central Saint Martins graduation collection through his celebrated tenures at Givenchy, Christian Dior, and Maison Margiela. Drawing heavily from The Costume Institute’s extensive archives, the exhibition features garments, accessories, sketches, research books, toiles, and culminates with his Spring/Summer 2024 Maison Margiela Artisanal presentation.The curation is organized into three distinct thematic sections: "Bearings," "Horizons," and "Atlas of Transformation." In addition to showcasing his technical mastery and artistic vision, the opening section "Bearings" will directly examine his 2010 and 2011 conduct, his dismissal from Dior, and the ongoing cultural dialogue surrounding accountability and legacy.John Galliano: Horizons will serve as the centerpiece for the 2027 Met Gala and will be open to the public at The Met Fifth Avenue from May 9, 2027 through January 9, 2028. items.title: Precious Okoyomon Unveils 25-Foot Teddy Bear Slide at MoMA PS1
items.text: Precious Okoyomon Unveils 25-Foot Teddy Bear Slide at MoMA PS1 Summary Artist Precious Okoyomon has unveiled an outdoor installation at New York's MoMA PS1The artwork features a wild garden, sound installations, and a giant teddy bear sculptureThe installation, the inaugural Courtyard Commission, will be on view for two years. For the next two years, the courtyard at MoMA PS1 will play host to Precious Okoyomon’s playground of pleasures. The New York-based artist, known for their lush gardenscapes and cute-creepy stuffed animal sculptures, has planted a living forest in even in the balmiest of New York heat for “Among the Flowers I Learned to Love: A Garden of Decreation,” their largest outdoor piece yet.Taking place on a plush bed of 1,500 perennials and plants, the installation is a sensorial blend of blooms, sculpture, and sound, co-cultivated with Rhode Island nursery issima. Oppositional species — native and invasive plants — grow beside one another, with pollinators and butterflies abound, creating a scene that challenges ideas of what can cultivate together.Okoyomon’s garden envisions life eternally in flux, inspired by philosopher Simone Weil’s concept of "decreation" — the constant making and unmaking of the world. As plants shift, seasons change, the space hones in on environmental and social realities of adaptation, resilience, and the unpredictable future of urban nature in shifting climates. View this post on InstagramA post shared by HypeArt (@hypeart)At the heart of the installation is “The Pleasure Principle,” a 25-foot-long sculpture. Visitors can climb into a teddy bear and listen to Okoyomon reading their poetry as they ride down a blood-red slide before exiting through its mouth. The adorable character is a recurring motif for the artist, often tied to idea(l)s of pleasure, while embodying the space between inner and outer worlds, à la Winnicott.“Among the Flowers I Learned to Love: A Garden of Decreation” (2026) is now on view for free in New York, and marks the inaugural piece of the museum’s experimental Courtyard Commissions series. items.title: DSM Kei Ninomiya Spotlights a Diverse Cast of Creatives for Its FW26 Campaign
items.text: DSM Kei Ninomiya Spotlights a Diverse Cast of Creatives for Its FW26 Campaign Summary DSM's Kei Ninomiya FW26 campaign features a diverse cast of international creatives Hiroshi Fujiwara, Hirokazu Kore-eda and more.The collection concept subverts football apparel, reworking sportswear into cultural expression.Available now across DSM flagships and online platforms. Dover Street Market and Kei Ninomiya have teamed up for a striking Fall/Winter 2026 campaign that highlights a diverse ensemble cast of international creatives. The campaign brings together artists, musicians, models and tastemakers from varied disciplines, spanning figures such as Hiroshi Fujiwara, acclaimed filmmaker Hirokazu Kore-eda, actress Miwako Ichikawa, costume designer Michiko Kitamura to Avu-Chan - the lead singer of alternative Japanese band Queen Bee - and more.At the core of the collection's concept is the subversion of football apparel, taking sports-derived garments beyond their traditional field settings and expanding them into a broader cultural language. By stripping these athletic motifs of their original context, the lineup transforms a strictly codified sport into a medium for free thinking and uninhibited expression. Designed as "clothes for nameless communities," the pieces break down the rigid boundaries of defined fanbases or subcultures, thus bending the rules within a sportswear framework.The DSM Kei Ninomiya FW26 range is now available across the retailers' flagships and online shops. View this post on Instagram A post shared by DSM Kei Ninomiya (@dsmkeininomiya) Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.title: A First Look at Nike and Zellerfeld’s 3D-Printed Air Works Prototype
items.text: A First Look at Nike and Zellerfeld’s 3D-Printed Air Works Prototype Name: Motoi Hatsuki Air Works 3D-printed SneakerSKU: TBCRelease Date: TBCNike has officially taken its first public step into the future of footwear manufacturing with its 3D-printed sneaker from its innovative Air Works Program, developed in partnership with additive manufacturing specialist Zellerfeld.Revealed via social media by Blue Room's Motoi Hatsuki, the prototype silhouette showcases a sleek, monochromatic model. The sneaker features a one‑piece 3D‑printed construction, eliminating traditional stitching and overlays for a streamlined, slip‑on profile. Hatsuki’s design draws inspiration from the Air Max 1000 and Tailwind V, incorporating exaggerated heel and forefoot Air bubbles, including a glowing neon yellow unit at the rear. The side panels showcase a paisley‑style looping motif, adding ornamental depth to the otherwise minimal structure. Branding is kept subtle, allowing the experimental form and texture to take center stage.As part of Nike’s broader Air Works initiative, which brought eight global creatives to Beaverton to collaborate with Nike engineers. Each participant will receive limited friends‑and‑family runs of their concepts, with previews rolling out ahead of Air Max Day 2027. View this post on Instagram A post shared by htk (@htk2626) Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.title: Official Images of the Nike Air Rejuven8 "Camo Pack"
items.text: Official Images of the Nike Air Rejuven8 "Camo Pack" Name: Nike Air Rejuven8 “Camo Pack”Colorway: “Black Camo,” “Barkroot Brown Camo”SKU: IU3167-002, IU3167-001MSRP: TBCRelease Date: August 2026Nike expands on the Air Rejuven8 revival, unveiling a bold new “Camo Pack” featuring two women’s-exclusive colorways in "Black Camo" and "Barkroot Brown." Originally introduced ahead of the 2008 Beijing Olympics as a post-performance recovery shoe for elite athletes, both new iterations retain the slip-on silhouette while introducing camouflage-inspired detailing across the molded, open-cell lattice cage.The "Black Camo" edition pairs a black knit bootie with tonal laces and foam tooling, contrasted by a semi-translucent shell patterned with smoky camouflage across its diamond cutouts. A crisp white Swoosh on the lateral side provides the only sharp break in color, keeping the palette sleek and understated. Meanwhile, the "Barkroot Brown Camo" version introduces warmth with a brown knit base beneath a glossy tortoiseshell-like-patterned cage, whose layered tones evoke the look of tortoiseshell. Black laces and a matching sole keep the design grounded, while a muted brown Swoosh subtly reinforces the earthy theme. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.title: The STEKA Octagonal Aluminum Pan Is Built for a Lifetime of Fire and Flame
items.text: The STEKA Octagonal Aluminum Pan Is Built for a Lifetime of Fire and Flame Summary ADDI designs the STEKA, an octagonal sauté pan for Mozambique, blending Scandinavian minimalism with Japanese craftsmanship.Features include a solid aluminum body, a removable handle and a drop-lid-inspired cover.Available now via Mozambique’s webstore, priced at around $172 USD. STEKA is an octagonal aluminum sauté pan designed by Swedish studio ADDI for Japanese cookware brand Mozambique. Conceived as a versatile cooking tool that bridges indoor kitchens and rugged outdoor environments, the pan was designed from a philosophy of structural logic and reduction rather than fleeting trends. Intended to transition seamlessly from a standard kitchen stove to an open campfire, the STEKA pan is engineered to be an adaptable, lifelong culinary instrument that ages and develops character alongside its owner.Crafted from 5 mm solid aluminum, STEKA offers heat retention similar to cast iron but with a lighter weight. Its high, straight sides expand cooking possibilities, while the removable cast‑aluminum handle, secured with a single stainless‑steel screw, allows for easy replacement, oven use, or compact storage. The companion lid, inspired by the Japanese otoshibuta drop‑lid, features raised points underneath that circulate moisture during simmering and braising, creating a self‑basting effect. Each piece is hand‑finished, with production limited to ten units per day, underscoring its artisanal quality.Available now via Mozambique's webstore, the STEKA pan retails at ¥27,500 JPY (approx. $172 USD) and comes with a five‑year warranty. items.title: Pharrell Williams’ JOOPITER Launches Its First-Ever Dedicated Watch Auction
items.text: Pharrell Williams’ JOOPITER Launches Its First-Ever Dedicated Watch Auction Summary JOOPITER debuts Keeping Measure: Watches & Timepieces, its first watch auction.Features collectible pieces from Patek Philippe, OMEGA, Cartier and more.Bidding is open until August 5, 2026, with highlights like the Alan Bean Speedmaster and HYT Moon Runner Red Magma. JOOPITER has announced its first auction under its newly established Watches Department, titled Keeping Measure: Watches & Timepieces. Curated to showcase both landmark models from storied Maisons and innovative creations from independent watchmakers, the sale spans over half a century of horological design. Featuring names such as Patek Philippe, Audemars Piguet, OMEGA, Piaget, Cartier, Ressence, HYT, Speake‑Marin and Ōtsuka Lotēc, the auction reflects the breadth of contemporary collecting and aims to appeal to seasoned collectors as well as newcomers.The auction is currently open for bidding until August 5, 2026, with highlights including rare OMEGA pieces such as a tropical dial 2915‑3 and the first auction appearance of the complicated Speedmaster Chrono Chime. Other standout lots include the OMEGA Alan Bean Speedmaster produced in 1969 and linked to the astronaut who became the fourth person to walk on the Moon; the Ulysse Nardin 18k Woven Bracelet Watch crafted by Gay Frères; as well as the HYT Moon Runner Red Magma -- a bold 2022 release showcasing HYT’s liquid‑time technology. Head over to JOOPITER's dedicated webpage to view the full lineup of the Keeping Measure: Watches & Timepieces sale. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.title: David Zwirner Announces a Two-Location Yoshitomo Nara Showcase in NYC
items.text: David Zwirner Announces a Two-Location Yoshitomo Nara Showcase in NYC Summary Yoshitomo Nara’s first David Zwirner exhibition opens in New York on October 29, 2026.The two-location exhibition features new atmospheric paintings and large-format drawings.The 19th Street location will feature thirteen monumental white bronze head sculptures. Opening this fall, David Zwirner will present Japanese artist Yoshitomo Nara’s inaugural solo exhibition with the gallery, spanning its 533 West 19th Street and 537 West 20th Street locations in New York. Marking the artist's first major solo presentation in the city in nearly a decade, the expansive showcase features new 2026 paintings, large-format drawings, recent sculptures and foundational early works from the 1980s chosen by Nara himself.The presentation at the 537 West 20th Street space highlights the latest stylistic shifts in Nara's two-dimensional artwork, featuring front-facing portraits with direct gazes rendered in a distinctly muted, highly nuanced color palette. The new paintings reveal intricate, diffused brushwork that builds richly atmospheric depths, alongside a fresh method where compositions are first sketched in colored pencil before receiving translucent washes of acrylic paint. In these works, figures adopt natural poses with tear-filled eyes that evoke a quiet sense of uncertainty. Exhibited in tandem are recent monochrome drawings created with industrial oil-based paint sticks, as well as his "line" paintings —works created by projecting and reanimating bold notebook sketches onto canvas to retain the rapid, fluid impulse of drawing.Concurrently, the 533 West 19th Street venue houses thirteen monumental bronze head sculptures created in 2024, each representing a ten-fold enlargement of palm-sized clay prototypes hand-molded by the artist. Coated in matte white urethane paint to afford an inviting visual softness, the large-scale works recall the "snow monsters" created by heavy snowfall during Nara's childhood winters. By magnifying the simple facial expressions of these small prototypes to a monumental scale, the installation explores the psychological impact of size, allowing the play of light and shadow across their smooth surfaces to foster an environment of serenity and reflection.Both showcases will take place across its aforementioned gallery locations starting October 29, 2026.
